# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1 (Bu-Vb Np1)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 1. The training rule on keeping extra robe-cloth beyond ten days

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathina* training rule, categorized as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1 in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya, stipulates that a monk who keeps extra robe-cloth (*cīvara*) for more than ten days commits an offense that requires both forfeiture of the cloth and confession [SuttaCentral]. Akira Hirakawa observes that this precept—often designated in the traditions by the key phrase "ten days"—is an obligation shared in common by both monks and nuns; because its complete formulation and commentary are set forth in the *Bhikkhu-vinaya*, the rule's analytical text is omitted in the Pali *Bhikkhunī-vinaya* [Hirakawa 1982]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying vibhaṅga has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels compiled on SuttaCentral confirm that the rule is represented across the Prātimokṣa and Vinayavibhaṅga literature of all major Buddhist Vinaya lineages, including Chinese, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Gāndhārī recensions preserved in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions, as well as the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes a passage-level parallel to the *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), an alignment verified by DharmaNexus, which computes an extensive shared section between the two texts (§2.1.1–2.15 matching Kd 8 §13.7.1–13.7.15 with 0.97 similarity) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally demonstrates substantial internal textual reuse across the Vinaya Piṭaka, particularly with other robe- and bowl-related rules such as Bu-Vb Np21, Bi-Vb Np1, and Bu-Vb Np3, as well as various Khandhaka chapters (Kd 15, Kd 11, Kd 2, Kd 13, and Kd 1) and commentaries like the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus reflect corresponding passages in Tibetan and Sanskrit Vinaya texts, including the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga*, *Prātimokṣasūtra*, and the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* [DharmaNexus].
